messages:
incident-bot: [PAGER] High error rate on streaming-decode cluster eu-west-1: decode-gpu-oom x5 in 2m. Affected service: gateway-streamer. Link: https://console.redwood/incident/2765432100
Maya (oncall): ack, paging in. Investigating. Anyone oncall for streamer infra?
Ravi: I'm online, seeing a ton of CUDA OOMs on nodes streamer-decode-*-p2. Logs show repeated `nvml: out of memory` during decode loop.
Derek: hit same, looks like a single customer runaway generation hitting max_tokens bypass — gateway is forwarding user max_tokens > 100k.
Jules: wait, how is gateway letting that through? We have a hard cap in config normally.
Maya (oncall): can someone confirm the incoming request headers/req body for one of the OOM traces?
Ravi: grabbing sample from logs... here's the req snippet: ```json
{"user_id":"acct-09","model":"rw-large","instructions":"...","max_tokens":500000}
```
Derek: omg 500k. That will exhaust KV cache + decode GPU mem. Gateway config shows `enforce_max_tokens: false` on the canary deployed last night. Looks like a regression from #PR-472.
Maya (oncall): action items: 1) patch gateway to re-enable hard cap + reject >20k tokens, 2) scale down/bounce affected decode pods to reclaim memory, 3) apply emergency token-throttling rule at the edge LB. Who takes what?
Ravi: I'll push a policy to the LB to inject `x-max-tokens:20000` for requests hitting /v1/stream and return 400 if client requests >20k. Patching now. Command: ```bash
kubectl -n gateway exec -it deploy/gw-nlb -- curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/_admin/ratelimit -d '{"route":"/v1/stream","max_tokens":20000}'
```
Derek: I'll roll back the canary that flipped `enforce_max_tokens` to false. Doing `kubectl -n gateway rollout undo deploy/gateway-canary --to-revision=14`
Jules: I'll start cordoning and restarting the top OOM nodes: `kubectl -n streaming delete pod streamer-decode-7c9b` and drain node if needed.
SRE-Bot: Automation triggered: scaling streamer-decode pool +25% (policy orange).
Maya (oncall): Ravi, status on LB rule?
Ravi: LB rule applied, returning 400 for >20k. Saw first rejects at 2765432127. That immediately dropped new runaway sessions.
Derek: rollback complete, gateway-canary back to rev14. Verified `enforce_max_tokens: true` in config.
Jules: restarted 6 pods, kernel logs look clean now. No further OOMs in last 30s.
Support-Liaison: heads-up: we have a high-volume customer (acct-09) that triggered this. Throttled ~12k streaming requests; some requests were dropped. Support has opened a ticket and will notify customer with mitigation summary.
Maya (oncall): Good. Postmortem items: revert PR-472 patch that disabled enforcement, add unit test for gateway that asserts rejection of >50k, and add alert for unusual client max_tokens distribution.
Ravi: Also suggest a runtime safety net: enforce per-user active token quota and prefix/KV memory accounting so single sessions can't hog GPU KV cache.
Derek: I'll prepare the rollback/prod-hotfix PR and ship a patch to hard-fail on >50k in code and add integration test.
Maya (oncall): timeline: incident opened 2765432100, LB rule at 2765432127, rollback 2765432135, last OOM observed 2765432138. Declaring immediate impact mitigated, keeping channel open for 30m for monitoring.
incident-bot: Incident status -> MITIGATED. Severity: Sev2. Runbook: streaming-gpu-oom.
Jules: monitoring looks stable. No new OOMs in 10m.
Support-Liaison: customer notified, ticket #INC-8890 created. No SLA breach expected but some requests were dropped; tracking exact count.
Maya (oncall): thanks all. Follow-ups: postmortem with timeline, root cause = canary config regression + missing gateway test, and follow up with SRE to add KV per-session accounting. Closing in 30m if stable. :white_check_mark:
